questions.question: Define and give one example of: (i) combination, (ii) decomposition, (iii) double displacement reactions.
questions.answer: (i) Combination: two or more reactants → one product. Example: 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO. (ii) Decomposition: one reactant → two or more products. Example: 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂. (iii) Double displacement: two compounds exchange ions. Example: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃.

questions.question: Distinguish thermal and photochemical decomposition with examples.
questions.answer: Thermal decomposition is driven by HEAT. Example: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (limestone heated). Photochemical decomposition is driven by LIGHT. Example: 2 AgCl → 2 Ag + Cl₂ (silver chloride turns grey in sunlight).

questions.question: Will the following displacement reactions occur? Justify briefly. (i) Cu + ZnSO₄, (ii) Fe + CuSO₄, (iii) Au + AgNO₃.
questions.answer: (i) Cu + ZnSO₄: NO. Copper is less reactive than zinc, so cannot displace it. (ii) Fe + CuSO₄: YES. Iron is more reactive than copper. Reaction: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. (iii) Au + AgNO₃: NO. Gold is less reactive than silver.
questions.explanation: Use the reactivity series: more reactive → can displace; less reactive → cannot.

questions.question: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 2 Al → 2 Fe + Al₂O₃, identify which substance is oxidised and which is reduced. Name the oxidising and reducing agents.
questions.answer: Aluminium (Al) is OXIDISED — it gains oxygen to form Al₂O₃. Iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) is REDUCED — it loses oxygen to form Fe. So Al is the REDUCING agent (it reduces Fe₂O₃) and Fe₂O₃ is the OXIDISING agent (it oxidises Al). This is the famous thermite reaction.
questions.explanation: Reducing agent loses oxygen; oxidising agent provides oxygen.

questions.question: Why does copper develop a green coating when exposed to moist air for a long time? How can this be cleaned?
questions.answer: Copper reacts with carbon dioxide and moisture in the air to form a layer of basic copper carbonate (greenish), which gives the green patina. To clean, use lemon juice or any mild acid — the citric acid reacts with the carbonate and removes the coating, restoring the shiny copper underneath.

questions.question: Why is rancidity a problem for the food industry, and what TWO measures are used to prevent it?
questions.answer: Rancidity makes oils and fats taste and smell bad and may produce harmful chemicals — making food unfit for consumption and harming the brand. Prevention measures: (1) airtight packaging that excludes oxygen (often flushed with nitrogen gas); (2) addition of ANTIOXIDANTS such as BHA, BHT; (3) refrigeration to slow oxidation. Any two are correct.

questions.question: For each reaction, balance and classify by type: (i) Na + Cl₂ → NaCl, (ii) HgO → Hg + O₂ (heated), (iii) Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂.
questions.answer: (i) 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl. Type: COMBINATION. (ii) 2 HgO → 2 Hg + O₂. Type: DECOMPOSITION (thermal). (iii) Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Type: DISPLACEMENT (Mg displaces H from HCl). All atoms balance on both sides.
questions.explanation: Three classic examples; identify type from form.

questions.question: Consider 2 Cu + O₂ → 2 CuO and CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. (i) Which is an oxidation reaction in everyday terms? (ii) Which is a reduction? (iii) Show that the second reaction is a redox reaction.
questions.answer: (i) The first reaction (2 Cu + O₂ → 2 CuO) is an oxidation reaction — copper gains oxygen. (ii) Looking at copper alone in the second reaction, CuO loses oxygen and becomes Cu — this is reduction (with respect to copper). (iii) The second reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O is a REDOX reaction because BOTH happen at the same time: CuO is reduced (loses O) AND H₂ is oxidised (gains O to form H₂O). Net: oxygen is transferred from CuO to H₂.
questions.explanation: Two reactions; the second is a textbook redox example.

questions.question: An iron gate left outside develops a layer of orange-brown rust over time. (i) Why does this happen — chemically? (ii) Why is rusting more rapid in coastal areas than in the desert? (iii) Suggest THREE ways to slow or prevent rusting.
questions.answer: (i) Iron reacts slowly with oxygen and moisture from air to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), commonly known as rust. The orange-brown colour is characteristic. (ii) Coastal areas have HIGH HUMIDITY (more moisture in the air) AND salt particles in the air, which act as electrolytes and accelerate the rusting reaction. Deserts are dry, so rusting is much slower. (iii) Three ways to prevent rust: (a) PAINTING — physical barrier between iron and air. (b) GALVANISING — coating with zinc, which corrodes preferentially (sacrificial protection). (c) ALLOYING — making stainless steel by mixing iron with chromium and nickel, which doesn't rust easily. (Other valid answers: oiling, electroplating with chromium, applying anti-rust spray.)
